profile.disclosure_policy: Confirmed directly on AWS own Global Infrastructure page (aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/): AWS does not publish specific street addresses or per-building technical specifications (square footage, power capacity in MW) for its data centers, as a matter of stated security and operational policy. AWS states each Region consists of a minimum of three isolated, physically separate Availability Zones, each with independent power, cooling, and physical security, but does not break this down to individual facility addresses. This session confirmed this disclosure policy directly rather than assuming it, and applies this finding to AWS records that otherwise have no facility specific address, square footage, planned capacity, or critical_it_mw on file. This is a company wide policy finding, not a statement that no such facility exists at this location.

reading.body:
Amazon IAD129 is a single building within AWS's Northern Virginia data center campus in Loudoun County, one of approximately 326 mapped facilities across Virginia. AWS does not publish power capacity, floor area, or technical specifications for individual buildings as a stated security policy, so this facility's contribution to AI workload capacity cannot be independently verified. The Northern Virginia region as a whole, spanning Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax counties, is reported by AWS to carry approximately 70 percent of global internet traffic and has absorbed $51.9 billion in AWS capital and operating investment from 2011 through 2021, with a further $35 billion announced for new campuses through 2040.

Virginia's 23 facilities with published megawatt figures total 1,375 megawatts. This facility ranks 24th by operator-disclosed capacity statewide, meaning it either publishes no figure or falls below the threshold of mapped sites with public specifications. Without published power data, the building cannot be sized against typical AI training densities.

AWS does not break regional capacity by individual Availability Zone or facility, so this building's role in serving AI compute cannot be isolated from the broader Northern Virginia footprint. Whether IAD129 hosts AI workloads, inference serving, or non-AI cloud services is not disclosed in any published source. Its relevance to grid constraints on AI scaling depends on the operator's allocation decisions, which remain private.
